solution: Disabled the sales report endpoint with its feature flag.
short_description: Orders API returned 503 errors due to database connection pool exhaustion caused by a new sales report endpoint running slow queries.
trigger: A new sales report endpoint held connections while it ran slow queries.
problem_statement: For 38 minutes orders-api could not get database connections and returned 503 on about 12% of checkout requests.
impact_description: orders-api could not get database connections and returned 503 on about 12% of checkout requests.
immediate_resolution: Disabled the sales report endpoint with its feature flag.

timeline.event: orders-api 4.18 released with the new sales report endpoint. None at the time.
Alert OrdersDbPoolExhausted fired. Logs showed PoolTimeout errors. On-call acknowledged and opened an incident channel.
20 of 20 pool connections in use per pod, most running the report query. Asked the database on-call to review long running queries.
timeline.action: Asked the database on-call to review long running queries.

timeline.event: Checkout still failing. Raised DB_POOL_MAX to 50 on orders-api.
Error rate back under 1%. Disabled the sales report endpoint with its feature flag.
timeline.action: Disabled the sales report endpoint with its feature flag.

root_causes: The sales report query held pool connections for up to 90 seconds with no statement timeout.
Reports and checkout shared one pool of 20 connections per pod, so reports could starve checkout.

action_items.action: Add an alert at 80% pool usage.
Set a 30 second statement timeout on report queries.
Move reports to a read replica with its own pool.
